accessibility_notes: Every Japanese line carries romaji and an English meaning.
The relationship schematic has a text equivalent on its file record and a short caption beside it on the lesson page.

The cover plate is illustration only: it has a text equivalent on its file record and the caption 'Cover plate — illustration, not a technical diagram.' beside it. Nothing in the course depends on seeing it.
The narration clip carries its Japanese line, romaji and English meaning as its text equivalent and as its lesson caption, and the lesson does not depend on hearing it.
Content files are UTF-8 without BOM; CJK line breaking and font fallback are renderer responsibilities.
attribution: Original teaching text, cover plate, schematic and narration: Coursebook demo pack. The cover plate and the schematic are host-composed, deterministic artwork built from the Atlas Lamp token palette; no third-party imagery is bundled. The narration clip is synthetic speech from Kokoro-82M voice jf_alpha (Apache-2.0), generated offline by the pack maintainer; no human speaker was recorded. Sources are cited by link and are not bundled; see sources[] and content/source-notes.md.
content_notes: Fresh verification: every Japanese wording and usage claim was re-read against the linked sources on 2026-11-06. No native-speaker review is recorded, and none is claimed.

Pack revision note: this pack now declares cb.pack v2 and links its two real assets through media[]. No Japanese wording changed in that revision, so the 2026-11-06 wording check still describes the language taught here. No new language or native-speaker review was performed for it.
L0 script policy: Japanese script is always paired with romaji and an English meaning. Romaji is a scaffold that fades; a romaji-only answer is not evidence of reading Japanese.
Register is taught as a function of addressee, relationship and setting, not as one correct translation of the English phrase 'I love you'.
Culture claims are kept narrow and attributed; regional, generational and personal variation is stated in the lesson rather than smoothed away.

One narration clip is bundled: content/narration-polite-confession.mp3, the polite first-confession line, synthesized offline on 2026-11-07 with Kokoro-82M voice jf_alpha (Apache-2.0), 24 kHz mono, encoded to 64 kbps MP3 with LAME 4.0. Its text equivalent carries the Japanese line, its romaji and its English meaning. Fading scaffold: the audio is a model of the line, not a substitute for the script or the romaji.

The fourth objective is a closed choice about a third situation, graded by exact comparison against its accepted registers. It is not a model-assessed explanation, and the pack claims no score for an open-response answer.

2.1.0 adds one composed cover plate (content/cover-plate.png), linked first in media[] so the Workshop storefront, the Library row and the course detail show the same plate. It is decorative illustration: it carries no register facts. The relationship map remains the pack's deterministic schematic and the only visual that states them. No wording, check or source changed.

files.description: Relationship and register map drawn deterministically for the demo pack.
files.text_equivalent: Schematic with three paths from speaker to register. You to a friend, affection, casual register (suki da yo). You to someone you respect, first confession, polite register (suki desu). You to a long-term partner, deep affection, intimate register (aishiteru). The schematic states that register is a function of addressee, relationship and setting.

media.caption: Pack visual — generated plate; not a diagram of the course.
好きです。付き合ってください。 (suki desu. tsukiatte kudasai.) — "I like you. Please go out with me."
Relationship and register map: friend to casual (suki da yo); respected addressee to polite (suki desu); long-term partner to intimate (aishiteru).

rubric: Chooses B as the romantic confession
Chooses A as affection between friends
Names a cue: the request 付き合ってください (tsukiatte kudasai), the polite です form, or the private setting
checks.stimulus: Two lines are shown. A: うん、好きだよ。 (un, suki da yo.) said to a friend after an outing. B: 好きです。付き合ってください。 (suki desu. tsukiatte kudasai.) said privately to someone the speaker is not yet close to. Which line is the romantic confession, and which cue makes it one?

evidence_criteria: Names which line is the romantic confession
Names which line is affection between friends
Points at the cue (form or request) that changes the reading
objectives.title: Tell everyday affection from a direct romantic declaration

rubric: Selects the polite 好きです line
Explains that the addressee is not close and the setting is deliberate
Does not select the intimate line for a first confession
checks.stimulus: Context: an adult speaker, an adult addressee they respect but do not know well, a private setting, a first confession, standard polite register. Which line from this pack fits, and why?

evidence_criteria: Selects the polite line for a first confession
Relates the choice to the addressee and setting
objectives.title: Choose the polite expression for a first confession

rubric: Produces 愛してる (aishiteru), in script or romaji
Does not produce the first-confession request
Keeps the setting private and the addressee a long-term partner
checks.stimulus: New context, no answer visible: you are at home with your spouse of ten years, in a private moment, and the feeling is settled and deep rather than new. Write the line you would use.

evidence_criteria: Produces the intimate line in a new, non-identical context
Does not reuse the first-confession line for a settled partnership
objectives.title: Recall the intimate declaration in a new context

rubric: Chooses the casual register for a close friend in public
Does not choose the polite or intimate register for that relationship
Keeps the choice tied to the addressee and the public setting
checks.stimulus: A close friend, in public, after an outing: you want to say something affectionate without making it a confession and without overstating the relationship. Which register fits? Answer A, B or C. A: casual register (suki da yo). B: polite register (suki desu). C: intimate register (aishiteru).

evidence_criteria: Picks the casual register for a close friend in public
Does not apply the intimate line to a friend in public
Reads the choice from the addressee and the public setting
objectives.title: Choose the register for a close friend in public

safety_notes: Audio is bundled and is synthetic. It is not a native-speaker pronunciation model, and this pack implements no listening check and no pronunciation score, so no listening evidence is claimed.
The topic is affection and confession, written for adult self-study; there is no explicit material.
